what: Behavioural cases for await_signals_with_quorum, shared by every SDK.
why: cleat#1132 was one defect written five times: every SDK passed the FULL name
set to await_signals_ms on every iteration, so a quorum counted deliveries
rather than distinct voters. Five copies of one algorithm cannot share an
implementation, so the fix is a sweep -- but the reason it went wrong five
times identically, and stayed wrong, is that nothing compared the SDKs.
This file is that comparison: one table, consumed by each SDK's own test
runner, so the next divergence fails somewhere rather than nowhere.
how: Each case drives the SDK's quorum loop against a scripted host and asserts
what the loop ASKED FOR on each iteration -- awaited_sets -- not only what
it returned. The narrowing is the mechanism; a test that checks only the
outcome passes against an implementation that fails for an unrelated reason.
host modes, and both are needed:
polite   -- delivers a queued name only while that name is still awaited,
which is what the engine's own DurableAwaitSignals does. This
exercises the NARROWING: a repeated name is never handed over
a second time, so the quorum fails as a timeout.
impolite -- delivers whatever is queued, ignoring the awaited set. This
exercises the OUT-OF-SET GUARD. A fix that rests only on the
polite case is a fix that rests on the host's manners.
error_kind is a semantic tag, never a message. The five SDKs word their
errors differently and always will; each test maps a kind to its own
substring. Asserting the string here would make this file a translation
table instead of a behavioural one.

error_kinds.unsatisfiable: min_count exceeds the size of the name set -- arithmetic forbids it
error_kinds.timeout: the deadline passed, or the host reported timed_out, short of quorum
error_kinds.out_of_set: the host delivered a name that is no longer awaited
error_kinds.rejections: more than max_rejections payloads carried {"rejected": true}

cases.name: one_name_voting_repeatedly_does_not_satisfy_a_quorum
cases.why: The defect itself: three deliveries of alpha satisfied a quorum of three with beta and gamma never sent.

cases.name: against_a_polite_host_the_repeated_name_is_never_delivered_again
cases.why: Same queue, a host that only delivers what is awaited. It must fail as a TIMEOUT: reaching the out-of-set guard here would mean the set had not narrowed.

cases.name: three_distinct_names_satisfy_a_quorum_of_three
cases.why: The partner case. Without it, 'three copies do not satisfy' is also true of an implementation that never satisfies a quorum at all.

cases.name: a_quorum_larger_than_its_name_set_is_refused_rather_than_timing_out
cases.why: Arithmetic forbids it, so it is a caller error, not a slow sender. It used to spin to the deadline and report 'got 0/4 signals'. awaited_sets is empty: the refusal must happen before any await.

cases.name: narrowing_does_not_edit_the_callers_name_set
cases.why: The narrowing must copy. The caller's collection may still be held by the workflow, and editing it in place is a defect the outcome cannot show.

cases.name: a_rejecting_voter_has_voted_and_leaves_the_set
cases.why: A rejection narrows too. max_rejections is 1 and alpha rejects twice, so an implementation that does NOT narrow counts two rejections and fails with kind 'rejections'. One that narrows never asks for alpha again, so the impolite second delivery is refused by the out-of-set guard instead. The two kinds are the discriminator: this case cannot be passed by accident.
